record.original_question: Given any choice of $m$-node tree tensor network (e.g., tensor train or Tucker) and choice of ranks (dimensions of edges in the tensor network), let the set of representable tensors in this tensor network be $S R^d_1 x *s x d_n$. Find a polynomial-time algorithm that takes as input any tensor $A R^d_1 x *s x d_n$ and yields an approximation $X S$ such that [ |X-A |_F^2 < (m-1) _Y S |Y-A |_F^2, ] or show that an $(m-1)$-approximation is optimal under complexity-theoretic assumptions.

evidence.quote: Given any choice of $m$-node tree tensor network (e.g., tensor train or Tucker) and choice of ranks (dimensions of edges in the tensor network), let the set of representable tensors in this tensor network be $S\subset \mathbb{R}^{d_1\times \cdots \times d_n}$. Find a polynomial-time algorithm that takes as input any tensor $\mathcal{A}\in\mathbb{R}^{d_1\times \cdots \times d_n}$ and yields an approximation $\mathcal{X}\in\mathbb{S}$ such that \[\|\mathcal{X}-\mathcal{A}\|_F^2 < (m-1)\min_{\mathcal{Y}\in S}\|\mathcal{Y}-\mathcal{A}\|_F^2,\] or show that an $(m-1)$-approximation is optimal under complexity-theoretic assumptions.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $n \geq 2$ and positive integers $d_1,\dots,d_n$ be given. A tree tensor network with $m$ nodes is specified by a tree $T$ with $m$ vertices, where $n$ of the leaves are labeled by the physical indices $1,\dots,n$ (with attached dimensions $d_1,\dots,d_n$), every internal edge $e$ is assigned a positive integer rank $r_e$, and each vertex $v$ carries a tensor whose modes correspond to the edges incident to $v$ (the dimension of a mode is $d_i$ for a physical leaf and $r_e$ for an internal edge). Contracting all internal edges yields a tensor in $\mathbb{R}^{d_1\times\cdots\times d_n}$. Let 
$$S \subset \mathbb{R}^{d_1\times\cdots\times d_n}$$
denote the set of all tensors representable by some assignment of node tensors with the prescribed tree structure and ranks. Familiar special cases include tensor trains and (hierarchical) Tucker decompositions.

The question: Either
(a) exhibit a polynomial-time algorithm (running in time polynomial in $\sum_i d_i$, $m$, and $\max_e r_e$) that, on input any tensor $\mathcal{A}\in\mathbb{R}^{d_1\times\cdots\times d_n}$, outputs $\mathcal{X}\in S$ satisfying
$$\|\mathcal{X}-\mathcal{A}\|_F^2 \;<\; (m-1)\,\min_{\mathcal{Y}\in S}\|\mathcal{Y}-\mathcal{A}\|_F^2,$$
where $\|\cdot\|_F$ denotes the Frobenius norm; or
(b) prove, under standard complexity-theoretic assumptions, that no polynomial-time algorithm can achieve an approximation ratio strictly better than $m-1$ for this problem.
artifact.status_search_result: Standard quasi-optimal algorithms (e.g., hierarchical/sequential SVD truncation for tensor trains and hierarchical Tucker) are known to give a $\sqrt{m-1}$-type bound on the error (i.e., factor $m-1$ in squared Frobenius norm), but no polynomial-time algorithm is known to beat this $(m-1)$ ratio, nor is there a complexity-theoretic lower bound proving optimality. Available literature on tree tensor network approximation and contraction-order optimization does not resolve this dichotomy.

status_evidence.title: Approximation theory of tree tensor networks (Nouy)
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses quasi-best approximation results for tree-based tensor formats with constants depending on the number of nodes.
status_evidence.claim: Standard quasi-optimal truncation gives a factor of (m-1) but no improvement is reported.

status_evidence.title: On the Optimal Linear Contraction Order of Tree Tensor Networks
status_evidence.snippet: Polynomial-time algorithm for optimal contraction order; does not address the low-rank approximation ratio question.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work on tree tensor networks does not resolve the (m-1)-approximation question.
